title: Cross-Site Scripting via Unescaped echo
platform_conditions: PHP 7.4/8.x; htmlspecialchars escapes single quotes only with ENT_QUOTES (default flags leave them raw), and default_charset is UTF-8 since PHP 5.6 — escaping breaks when the output document charset differs
security_mechanism: echo/print place the bytes into the HTML response verbatim, so markup in the input becomes live document structure. htmlspecialchars() with default flags escapes < > & and double quotes but not single quotes, so values landing inside single-quoted attributes (onmouseover='...') still execute; with a non-UTF-8 document charset, multi-byte sequences can consume the quote character and defeat the escaping. header('Location: '. $input) refuses to emit CR/LF since PHP 5.1.2, so the surviving defect there is the unvalidated open redirect — an attacker URL that launderes phishing and OAuth-style flows through the trusted origin.

source_sink_clues.source: Reflected query parameters, stored user content rendered into pages, and redirect target parameters.
source_sink_clues.sink: echo/print of unescaped request data; htmlspecialchars calls without ENT_QUOTES or with a charset mismatched to the document; header('Location: '.attacker_url)

tracking_guards: Require htmlspecialchars($v, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') (flags explicit) for HTML body context and context-appropriate encoding elsewhere (urlencode in URLs, attribute-safe encoding in quoted attributes); require redirect targets validated against a fixed host allowlist or constrained to site-relative paths.
not_candidate_when: Output is escaped with ENT_QUOTES under a charset that matches the document, the response is non-HTML (JSON served with an explicit application/json Content-Type), or redirect targets are site-relative or allowlisted after validation.
public_references: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html
CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html
OWASP Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
